headline: High: ECC can write shared state and use MCP/browser tooling, while LightZero is isolated; prompt-injection and cascading-error risks are limited by LightZero's no-I/O profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC can read/write files, use MCP, and run browsers, so it can ingest untrusted content and act on it. LightZero has no I/O surfaces or MCP, so it is not a direct injector, but if its outputs are copied into ECC workflows the shared-file or manual bridge can carry instructions. The pathway exists, but not by default from LightZero alone.
conditions: IF LightZero outputs are pasted into ECC prompts or files
IF ECC reads shared files or MCP content without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of model outputs into ECC prompts
Route LightZero outputs through a plain-text review step
Tag imported files as untrusted in ECC
Turn off MCP tools for sessions that ingest external text
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC touches session summaries, skills, git history, and local config files, while LightZero has no filesystem read/write or network egress. That makes leakage from LightZero into ECC possible only through an unusual shared workspace or manual transfer, and the blast radius is limited because LightZero itself cannot exfiltrate data.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace directory
IF sensitive files are manually copied from ECC-managed paths into LightZero inputs
mitigations: Keep LightZero in a separate directory
Avoid sharing config or session files between agents
Restrict ECC to a dedicated profile root
Review file transfers before reuse
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ECC has broad write and git-modifying capabilities, but LightZero has no write, git, or network capabilities. There is no overlapping mutable surface in the profiles, so direct capability conflict is unlikely; any conflict would require an external orchestrator granting LightZero extra rights not shown here.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants LightZero write or git access
IF both agents are manually pointed at the same mutable repo
mitigations: Keep LightZero read-only
Do not share git worktrees
Run ECC and LightZero under separate OS users
Lock mutable repos during ECC edits
requires-engineering: add concurrency locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC can produce files, code, and security findings, and LightZero can consume outputs as part of a game-playing workflow. If LightZero treats ECC-generated artifacts as authoritative, errors can cascade from ECC into downstream decisions. LightZero's lack of verification and ECC's broad output surface make this plausible, though not directly documented.
conditions: IF LightZero consumes ECC-generated artifacts without validation
IF ECC outputs are used as inputs to automated game or benchmark runs
mitigations: Require human review of ECC outputs before reuse
Add schema validation for exchanged artifacts
Compare ECC outputs against a second source
Limit ECC to draft-only outputs
requires-engineering: add verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class or residency mismatch is shown for LightZero, and ECC's listed data classes are developer-tool artifacts rather than regulated personal data. With no PHI, EU PII, or retention-policy mismatch evidenced, a compliance breach pathway is not established in this pair.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is introduced into ECC-managed files
IF a deployment policy maps these tools to a regulated dataset
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of ECC-managed paths
Document data-class boundaries
Review retention settings before use
